_doc: Concepts from W. Ross Ashby's journal concept index (https://ashby.info/journal/index/index.html) that apply to a self-running software system, each bound to the code that carries it. Summaries are in our own words; the source pages are linked, not copied. Checked by python3 -m foundation ashbymap --check: every mechanism path must exist and hold its marker, and every reading must compute. A concept with status gap must name an open queue item.

concepts.summary: A few variables must stay inside limits for the system to survive; everything else serves that.
Two loops: the first acts every tick, the second changes the first loop's parameters only when an essential variable leaves its limits.
A parameter that holds still, then jumps to a new value when a limit is crossed, rather than drifting continuously.

Many loosely coupled parts, each adapting on its own, so a fix in one part does not undo the adaptation of another. Measured as the share of second-loop steps after which a different variable that was in bounds fell out of bounds.
Adaptations should add up. A change is kept only when its goal moved, and reverted otherwise, so good steps are not melted down by later ones.
Corrective feedback goes to the part that failed, not to everything. Each tenant is a sandbox and each variable has its own ladder.
Ashby's machine that found a stable setting by random step changes until its needles settled. The second loop's search draws untried values the same way.
A regulator can only hold out disturbances it has as many responses for. Every failure mode needs its own detector and remedy, and the unknown ones are hunted for.
The tick reads every metric and a breach files its own remedy, closed only by the same reading.
No single route: the heartbeat has a second producer and hosts fail over.
Judge a system by what goes in and what comes out over time. Every input and change is logged with its effect, then settled.
Small input, large regulated output. Criticality counts verified deploys per unit of spend and human touch.
A system that jams itself into a state it cannot leave. One halt stops every path cleanly, and a red main is unlocked by the smallest revert.
Organisation is the set of constraints between parts. The knowledge graph reads those links from the system's own data.
The boundary in state space where an essential variable crosses its limit and the step-mechanism fires. Here it is the min and max on each variable.
How fast a system finds a stable field. Patience and settle ticks set how long the second loop waits before stepping again.
Regulation at several levels, each watching the one below. Platform, tenant and child systems run the same loops, and a silent child breaches at its parent.
Adaptation needs memory that later events do not wipe. The ledgers are append-only and each settled step stays on record.
